newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends up in quiet trade ahead of data.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends up in quiet trade ahead of data.

text.p: The key March three-month Euroyen contract on TIFFE ended firmer on Thursday in subdued trade ahead of widely watched May industrial output data due on Friday, traders said.

The March's turnover fell to 38,421 contracts on Thursday from Wednesday's 138,498. Most traders were still licking their wounds from Wednesday's nosedive on the results of the Bank of Japan's quarterly "tankan" survey of corporate sentiment.

"We're expecting rises in (Japan May) output data (due out on Friday), but most traders were wary of holding fresh speculative positions because many of them have just been knocked down on Wednesday after the tankan, as they had been wrongly positioned for it," a trader at a city bank said.
May industrial output data and forecasts for June and July will be released on Friday at 1.30 p.m. (0430 GMT).
Economists polled by Reuters forecast increases in May output ranging from 1.2 percent to three percent, compared with a revised month-on-month drop of 0.5 percent in April.
"If the output shows a rise of over two percent, that would become a sell factor for the Euroyen," said a trader at a long-term bank.
The market is also wary of being positioned heavily ahead of a speech by BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita on Friday.
Matsushita will give the speech to corporate managers from 12.40 p.m. (0340 GMT) on Friday.

In the cash market, the key three-month certificates of deposit (CD) were issued at 0.64 percent, the highest rate since August 9, 1996, traders said. The issue volume was around 100 billion yen. It was issued at 0.63 percent on Wednesday.
On the technical front, the March finished Thursday's session at well above its key 20-day moving average of 98.73 on Thursday.
Traders said if the March decisively breaches the support, it could slide further to around the next major chart support of 98.50 in the medium term. A minor support also lies at 98.60, they said.
"With March's tumble to 98.50, the market would fully price in a half-point rise in the discount rate," said a brokerage trader.
